$doc: Canonical card space — THE datum. Four numbers, and nothing else in foilkit
may type a fifth: every raster size, aspect and corner radius is COMPUTED
from these, in packages/core/src/canonical-space.ts, which the browser
renderer, the node authoring stack and the rectifier all import.
Why a JSON file and not four TypeScript constants: this is a MEASUREMENT, and
measurements are CC0 while code is MIT (see REUSE.toml). The split is by file,
so the datum is a file. It also predates the extraction: DeckPal needed a
datum both of its apps could read off disk, because its api tsconfig pinned
rootDir and could not import its web sources. That constraint is gone — there
is one derivation module now, not two — but a JSON datum with its provenance
beside it remains the right shape.
PROVENANCE. A standard Pokemon TCG card measures 63 x 88 mm. That footprint
is well attested: it is the nominal 2.5in x 3.5in poker/trading-card size,
reported unchanged from the game's 1996 launch through current standard-size
cards, and it is the trim an officially licensed accessory (Ultra Pro
standard deck protectors) is sized to fit.
The 3 mm corner radius is TRIANGULATED, NOT OFFICIAL. It is inferred from a
Japanese trading-card die-cutting specification that documents a 63 x 88 mm
trim with 'R3' (3 mm) corners for that poker-size card, plus a Pokemon-
specific size guide. A second manufacturing source quotes 2.5 mm for
'standard card corners', and a Pokemon-specific source notes the radius
varies slightly between print runs and eras. The credible range is therefore
2.5-3.0 mm; NO TPCi factory die specification is published, so 3 mm is the
best-supported point estimate rather than an authoritative figure. Treat it
as 'the corner the box should round to' and not as a claim about any
individual physical card.
pxPerMm 8 is chosen so the canonical raster comes out INTEGRAL in both axes
(63*8 = 504, 88*8 = 704) and strictly larger IN BOTH AXES than the mask
authoring raster the whole corpus was drawn at (490x674) — so the corpus
migration resampled up and nothing was downsampled. It is deliberately NOT
chasing the catalog scan rasters (600x825/600x837/600x838): those are wider,
but a mask is a soft-edged zone map carrying 0.008 UV of feather, not a scan,
and 8 px/mm is the coarsest density that stays integral.
